answer.question: What should I decide before choosing a Ponte Vedra Beach putting green?
answer.answer: Choose the putts, chipping space and walking room you want, then identify the usable area around trees and water. Confirm any Ponte Vedra zoning-district requirements and your community’s architectural-review process before finalizing the footprint.

blocks.h2: Build around the shots you want to repeat.
paras: A few useful putting lines close to the house can make regular practice easy. Discuss contours, cups and fringe after choosing the distances that matter to you. Select the roll and breaks for the practice you want to repeat.
On a golf- or lagoon-facing lot, keep the property boundary, water setback and walking access in the plan. A lawn or pet area can remain separate from the putting surface.

blocks.h2: Check the zoning district and private requirements.
paras: The Ponte Vedra Boulevard corridor includes properties within the county’s Ponte Vedra Zoning District, with its own yard and open-space rules. Confirm the parcel and intended work with county planning before using a general county limit to size the project.

In Sawgrass, Marsh Landing or The Plantation, obtain the current architectural instructions as well. Private review does not replace applicable public requirements. Bring the written conditions, tree information and any drainage concerns to the estimate.

blocks.h2: Practice for greens Pete Dye built, in your own back yard.
paras: TPC Sawgrass has been the permanent home of THE PLAYERS Championship since 1982, played every March on Pete Dye's Stadium Course, whose par-3 17th is the island green; Dye's Valley Course is its neighbor (Wikipedia: TPC Sawgrass). The PGA TOUR's world headquarters is in Ponte Vedra Beach, and so is the ATP Tour's.

The courses around it run just as deep. Sawgrass Country Club, member-owned and founded in 1974, hosted THE PLAYERS on its Ed Seay course from 1977 to 1981 (Wikipedia: Sawgrass Country Club). The Ponte Vedra Inn & Club, the 1928 resort that started the town, has Ocean and Lagoon courses reworked by Bobby Weed, and The Plantation plays 18 holes, par 72, over 7,141 yards.

A backyard green won't be the 17th, but it's where a short game gets its reps: real slope to read, a collar, and cups wherever you'd like them, on a layout designed for your yard, which you sign off before work starts. On golf-frontage lots the yard usually falls toward the course or a lagoon, and we build the base to use that fall.

blocks.h2: Two approval paths: the zoning board on the boulevard, a private committee behind the gates.
paras: Ponte Vedra Beach is unincorporated, with no city hall, but it has its own zoning district. The Ponte Vedra Zoning District Regulations, Ordinance 2020-38, are administered by the Ponte Vedra Zoning and Adjustment Board, which takes final action on building size, land-use intensity, and the yards and open space around buildings (Ponte Vedra Zoning District Regulations).

The zoning rules date to 1965, and the overlay for the coastal corridor to 1997. On the boulevard, where many older lots have no HOA in the usual sense, ask county planning whether your layout needs anything from the board before it's final.

Inside Sawgrass Players Club, Sawgrass Country Club, Marsh Landing and The Plantation, a private architectural committee approves changes instead, and the covenants still bind. Our guide explains what a committee can and can't stop.

blocks.h2: Salt air, brackish wells and live-oak shade: three reasons grass gives out near the ocean.
paras: Onshore salt spray burns St. Augustine and Zoysia along the Ponte Vedra Boulevard corridor, and irrigation drawn from shallow coastal wells can be brackish enough to make it worse. Turf takes neither.

Mature live oaks and cabbage palms shade much of the boulevard corridor and the older Sawgrass streets, and grass under them never gets the sun it needs. Turf needs none, and the canopy keeps its surface temperature well down in summer (what shade does for turf).

The sand has a past, too. The town began as Mineral City, a titanium and mineral-sands mining settlement after a 1914 discovery, and the National Lead Company renamed it Ponte Vedra in 1929 (Wikipedia).

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Ponte Vedra Beach, FL?
faq.a: We install backyard putting greens, artificial turf and pet turf in Ponte Vedra Beach, FL. On the Ponte Vedra Boulevard corridor, yards sit inside the county's Ponte Vedra Zoning District; behind the gates at Sawgrass, Marsh Landing and The Plantation, a private architectural committee decides. Salt air and live-oak shade, hard on grass here, don't touch turf. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: When and where does the Ponte Vedra Zoning and Adjustment Board meet?
faq.a: On the first Monday of each month at 3:00 p.m., in the County Auditorium at 500 San Sebastian View, St. Augustine (St. Johns County boards). Its members are appointed by the St. Johns County Board of County Commissioners.

faq.q: Will turf count against my lot's impervious surface ratio?
faq.a: St. Johns County's code counts compacted material only where it's used for parking or as a road, and a lawn is neither; the code never mentions artificial turf (St. Johns County Land Development Code). The Ponte Vedra Zoning District has regulations of its own, so keep your base's permeability details on hand and confirm with county planning before anything is ordered.

faq.q: Does Florida's turf law override the ARC in Marsh Landing or Sawgrass?
faq.a: No. Since 19 May 2026 a county ban on standard-compliant turf has been off the table for single-family lots up to an acre (Fla. Stat. 125.572), but DEP's own FAQ says the rule leaves HOA rules, deed restrictions and private agreements alone (DEP). And a yard facing a fairway is in view of a community golf course, where Fla. Stat. 720.3045 leaves the committee its say (Fla. Stat. 720.3045).
